transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Verdant Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Marco Ruiz (CTO)
---
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Samira from our Optimize team. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya Nair: Good, thanks. Excited to see the quant stuff, we've been debating INT8 vs FP8 for a while.
[00:18] Samira Khan: Great. Quick agenda: we'll run through the Optimize console, show quant profiles (INT8/FP8), show quality vs latency charts from our internal and public benchmarks, and then map to a pilot plan for Verdant. Sound OK?
[00:31] Marco Ruiz: Yep. Also want to cover security/KMS integration briefly.
[00:35] Samira Khan: Yep we'll hit that.
[00:38] Jordan Patel: Cool. Samira, if you want to share screen, show the Optimize UI?
[00:42] Samira Khan: Sharing now... all right, can you see the console?
[00:46] Priya Nair: Yep, seeing it. UI looks similar to the demo we saw earlier.
[00:51] Samira Khan: Awesome. So this is the quantization profile page in Redwood Optimize. We have prebuilt profiles for INT8, FP8, and mixed precision. The idea is we provide target latency buckets and a quality threshold — Optimize suggests profiles and runs small evals against your eval set.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Quick Q — when you say FP8, do you mean hardware FP8 or simulated? On our infra we care about GPU support.
[01:20] Samira Khan: Good question. For hosted we run on hardware that has FP8 support when available; for Dedicated/Private we detect hardware capabilities and pick the best kernel. If hardware doesn't support FP8 natively, we use optimized simulation paths — there's a small perf hit, but quality is the same. We annotate that in the profile.
[01:39] Priya Nair: And INT8 typically gives how much latency improvement vs FP16? Ballpark numbers for a 13B model?
[01:46] Samira Khan: Ballpark for a 13B on typical A100/V100-ish hardware: INT8 gives ~1.8x throughput and ~30-45% lower p99 latency depending on sequence length; FP8 can be similar or slightly better on newer GPUs with proper kernels. Important caveat: INT8 quant can introduce quality regressions depending on model and tasks; that's where our per-profile evals and delta scoring come in.
[02:10] Jordan Patel: To add, in our experience for classification and embeddings tasks INT8 usually is safe, while for long-context generation or instruction-following, FP8 often preserves quality better.
[02:22] Marco Ruiz: Any examples of quality metrics? BLEU? Human eval?
[02:26] Samira Khan: We provide automated metrics — task-dependent. For summarization we'd show ROUGE / BERTScore; for instruction correctness we use a passed/fail rubric and small human evals if needed. The console shows delta vs FP16 baseline.
[02:40] Priya Nair: Could you show a concrete chart?
[02:44] Samira Khan: Sure — toggling to the 'quality vs latency' tab. Here's a scatter: x-axis is p50 latency, y-axis is relative quality (BERTScore). Each point is a profile — you can see FP16 baseline, FP8 points slightly left (lower latency) with small quality drop, INT8 points further left but with a wider spread in quality.
[03:05] Priya Nair: Hmm okay I see some dots where INT8 has >2% BERTScore drop on certain prompts. That's concerning for our summarization use case.
[03:14] Samira Khan: Totally. For summarization we often recommend starting with FP8 or mixed precision. We also support hybrid routing: route 10% of traffic to FP16 for high-precision outputs (e.g., long docs) and use INT8 for quick responses, or fall back to FP16 on low-confidence outputs via our confidence scoring.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: The hybrid routing — is that a runtime cost? How do you implement fallback without killing latency?
[03:39] Samira Khan: It's implemented as part of the serving runtime: prefix caching and KV cache allows us to warm the FP16 variant quickly. Fallback only triggers on a subset of tokens and we have a policy for fallback thresholds. There's some added tail latency when fallback is invoked but overall cost is lower and quality SLOs are preserved.
[04:00] Marco Ruiz: On the security side — VPC and KMS. We need assurance that keys never leave our KMS.
[04:07] Jordan Patel: We have Private deployment and Dedicated options; with Private you control the control plane in VPC and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We'll share the SOC2 docs and a KMS integration guide after the call.
[04:19] Priya Nair: Good. Also curious about audit logs — request-level logs and token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback.
[04:27] Samira Khan: Yep, Console has request-level traces and token-level billing; for Dedicated we can surface these into your SIEM.
[04:34] Priya Nair: Nice.
[04:36] Jordan Patel: Back to quant — Samira, can you demo the process of running a quick profile against a sample eval set?
[04:42] Samira Khan: Sure. I'm uploading a small eval set — in a pilot we'd use Verdant's eval set. For demo I have a public summarization set. Selecting 'target p50=150ms' and quality threshold 0.98 relative to FP16... kick off run. This spawns a lightweight batch that runs across profiles.
[05:07] Samira Khan: Results streaming in... look at the table: profile name, p50, p95, relative quality, cost estimate. See INT8_profile_1: p50 95ms, rel quality 0.96; FP8_profile_1: p50 120ms, rel quality 0.985.
[05:27] Priya Nair: So FP8 hits our quality bar with ~20% latency gain vs FP16. That aligns with what we'd prefer.
[05:33] Marco Ruiz: What's the variability across prompts? We saw some outliers.
[05:37] Samira Khan: We show distribution and worst-case prompts; Optimize also flags prompts with >X% drop so you can review and either add prompt-specific overrides or route them to a higher precision variant.
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot, we'll want to run at our expected QPS and sequence lengths. Can you simulate that?
[05:55] Samira Khan: Yes — the pilot package includes a load-gen harness we can run in Dedicated or against Hosted endpoints. We'll need your target QPS, sequence length distribution, and a sample dataset.
[06:06] Priya Nair: We'll compile that and send to Liam.
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: I'll provide the QPS and a snippet of infra constraints.
[06:12] Jordan Patel: Great. Any objections to timeline? We suggested pilot wk of Dec 15.
[06:17] Marco Ruiz: That works. We need pricing though — especially Dedicated commit sizing.
[06:21] Jordan Patel: I'll send pricing and commit tiers after this call.
[06:25] Priya Nair: One more — model compatibility. We mostly run a fine-tuned 13B Llama variant. Is Redwood Optimize compatible?
[06:32] Samira Khan: Yes — we support a wide range of LLMs including Llama variants. For fine-tuned weights we do an onboarding step to generate per-layer quant profiles; sometimes we recommend minimal calibration steps. We'll include guidance in the onboarding checklist.
[06:48] Priya Nair: Any gotchas with instruction-following models?
[06:51] Samira Khan: Instruction tuning can be more sensitive to quant; FP8 tends to be safer. Also watch out for generation length — longer sequences can amplify quantization errors. Our reports show per-sequence-length deltas so you can decide.
[07:06] Jordan Patel: Cool. We're about 40 minutes in; quick recap and next steps?
[07:11] Priya Nair: Please send security docs and pricing. We'll send sample eval and QPS. Pilot week of Dec 15.
[07:17] Jordan Patel: Perfect. Samira — action item?
[07:20] Samira Khan: I'll run an INT8 vs FP8 bench on Verdant sample once they send it and share the detailed plots (due 2026-12-17).
[07:28] Jordan Patel: I'll send pricing and Dedicated options tomorrow (due 2026-12-09).
[07:33] Liam O'Connor: I'll get sample dataset specs and QPS to you by Friday (due 2026-12-10).
[07:38] Marco Ruiz: Thanks all, looking forward.
[07:40] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pilot plan and docs.
---
